papers.title: Bayesian Model Selection Methods for Mutual and Symmetric $k$-Nearest Neighbor Classification
papers.abstract: The $k$-nearest neighbor classification method ($k$-NNC) is one of the simplest nonparametric classification methods. The mutual $k$-NN classification method (M$k$NNC) is a variant of $k$-NNC based on mutual neighborship. We propose another variant of $k$-NNC, the symmetric $k$-NN classification method (S$k$NNC) based on both mutual neighborship and one-sided neighborship. The performance of M$k$NNC and S$k$NNC depends on the parameter $k$ as the one of $k$-NNC does. We propose the ways how M$k$NN and S$k$NN classification can be performed based on Bayesian mutual and symmetric $k$-NN regression methods with the selection schemes for the parameter $k$. Bayesian mutual and symmetric $k$-NN regression methods are based on Gaussian process models, and it turns out that they can do M$k$NN and S$k$NN classification with new encodings of target values (class labels). The simulation results show that the proposed methods are better than or comparable to $k$-NNC, M$k$NNC and S$k$NNC with the parameter $k$ selected by the leave-one-out cross validation method not only for an artificial data set but also for real world data sets.

summary_zh.motivation: 改进k近邻分类方法，处理互邻与对称邻域。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance k-nearest neighbor classification by incorporating mutual and symmetric neighbship.
summary_en.method: Bayesian mutual and symmetric k-nearest neighbor regression using Gaussian processes with new label encodings.
summary_en.result: Proposed methods outperform or match traditional k-NN and its variants on both artificial and real datasets.
summary_en.validation: Compared against leave-one-out cross-validated k-NN on synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets.
